summary: Count out loud to 100 by ones and by tens.
Understand that a number tells how many objects are in a set of up to 10.
Use ordinal words (first, second...) to tell an object's place in a line of up to 10.
Recognize how many objects (up to 10) are in a group without counting, in any arrangement.
Count forward from any number up to 20, with or without objects.
Read, write, say and show whole numbers 0 to 20.
Find the number one more or one less than a number up to 10.
Compare and order numbers 0 to 10, with and without objects, using more, less, equal.

Share a set of objects fairly into two or more equal groups.
Name pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters.

Fill the outline of a big flat shape with smaller shapes.
Build larger structures from solid shapes.
Use basic shapes to represent real-world objects.
Compare objects by length, size, weight and position using words.
Put up to 6 objects in order by length or weight.
Find attributes objects share and sort them into sets.
Compare how many objects it takes to fill two different containers.
Use everyday time words like yesterday, today, tomorrow, morning and night.
Collect and organize information about objects and events around them.
Make real-object graphs and picture graphs from category data.
Answer questions and draw conclusions from real-object and picture graphs.

Count forward with objects from any number to 100 by 1s, 2s, 5s and 10s.
Count forward without objects by 1s, 2s, 5s and 10s up to 100.
Find 10 more or 10 less than a number up to 100.
Compare and order whole numbers from 0 to 100.
Place a whole number up to 20 on an open number line.
Describe how numbers compare using more than, less than and equal to.
Show and solve addition and subtraction problems within 10.

Split a regular polygon with models and tell when the parts are equal.
Share a set of objects equally into two or three groups.
Name pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters and state their values.
Write a coin's value using the cent sign.

Put small flat shapes together to make a larger named shape.
Build structures from solid shapes.

Find 10 or 100 more or less than a three-digit number.
Use objects to tell whether a number is even or odd.
Round numbers up to 1,000 to the nearest ten and hundred.

Estimate sums and differences up to 100.

Solve addition and subtraction problems with numbers up to two digits.

Show and describe repeating shape patterns.

Sort solid shapes by number of faces, vertices and edges.

Use a ruler to measure to the nearest whole unit, linking ruler marks to length.

Tell the difference between a.m. and p.m.
Read and write time to the quarter hour on analog and digital clocks.

Measure length to the nearest centimeter or quarter inch.

Find elapsed time.
Convert between seconds, minutes, hours and days.
